summary: Sustained elevated 5xx floor for customer during mixed embeddings+chat burst: connection oscillation -> runtime GC/eviction thrash
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 18:45 UTC BrightDocs reported persistent ~5-8% 5xx rate on mixed-embedding and chat routes for their tenant. Errors manifest as 502/503 from api-gateway and upstream runtime connection errors. Impact: production traffic for BrightDocs degraded, intermittent user-facing failures for document ingestion and chat features. Environment: prod-us-east, enterprise tenant (BrightDocs), traffic mix: 60% small chat requests, 40% batched embedding uploads (small/medium).

Observed behavior: When BrightDocs client increases concurrent connections and aggressively reconnects after failed requests, api-gateway 5xx floor rises and remains elevated for ~10-30 minutes before gradually recovering. During elevated period: runtime worker logs show repeated small process OOMs, kvcache eviction storms, and frequent shard reloads (cold-shard events). Apigw logs show 'upstream reset' or 'no healthy upstream' followed by 502/503 responses.

Steps to reproduce (partial/operational):
1) Simulate mixed traffic: parallel 250 concurrent chat calls (short prompts) + parallel upload of 10k small embedding batches (size ~128 vectors) across 120s window.
2) Client aggressively retries on 5xx with short backoff (<200ms) and re-opens new connections per retry.
3) Observe accept-queue growth at apigw, followed by connection churn to runtime and small OOM/restart events in runtime logs.

Relevant logs/metrics:
- APIGW traces: link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ingress/apigw-traces?orgId=1&var-tenant=brightdocs (request ids: req-20260313T1848-0a1b, req-20260313T1851-4f2c)
- Runtime logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/runtime/2026-03-13/worker-23.log (OOMs and shard reload stack traces)
- KVcache metrics: kvcache.evictions/sec spike coincident with OOMs: 1200 -> 8500
- Host metrics: container RSS climb briefly before OOM, then restart and rapid reconnects

Initial customer note: "We started seeing errors after our nightly batch ramped up retries. UX shows failed uploads and chat messages not returning. Happened twice in the last 24 hours."
comments: 2026-03-13 19:05 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged. Collected tenant and trace IDs and escalated to SRE. Asked customer to pause aggressive retries if possible while we investigate.

2026-03-13 19:18 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Observed accept queue growth at APIGW and connection churn to runtime. Several runtime workers reported small OOMs; kvcache evictions very high. Adding backpressure at edge could help immediate mitigation.

2026-03-13 19:31 - Support (Ava Chen): Informed customer to temporarily throttle client retries and increase retry backoff to 1s. Customer applied change and reported partial reduction in errors after 6 minutes.

2026-03-13 19:55 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Deployed temporary ingress rate-limiter rule for tenant brightdocs to cap concurrent connections (cap=120) and enabled soft-priority-shedding on their route. Monitoring for stabilization.

2026-03-13 20:12 - Customer (BrightDocs SRE - Lina Park): Confirmed error rate dropped to ~0.8% after throttling. Concerned about future bursts due to our ingestion pattern — requesting long-term fix.

2026-03-14 09:02 - Engineering (Samir Patel): Noted related PR implementing kvcache eviction smoothing and improved shard reload backoff: PR #4123. Planning canary to reduce hot reloads induced by transient connection storms.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Aggressive client reconnect pattern produced connection oscillation that amplified ingress accept-queue and produced short-lived hot fanout to runtime workers, causing kvcache growth and GC pressure -> small OOMs and restart loop.
Hypothesis 2: KV cache eviction policy interacts poorly with mixed embeddings and chat request shapes: embedding warmups allocate larger kv entries triggering eviction storms under connection churn.
Evidence: High kvcache.evictions/sec correlates with OOM timestamps in runtime logs. Worker restarts align with apigw accept-queue peaks. No clear kernel or driver faults in node-level logs.

Temporary mitigations tried: asked customer to soften retry policy; applied tenant-level ingress soft cap (concurrent conn cap=120); enabled priority-shedding on embed-heavy route. Observed >5x reduction in kvcache eviction spikes and drop in 5xx rate from ~6% to ~0.9%.
Repro steps validated in staging: Simulated client with short retry backoff reproduces accept-queue oscillation and leads to kvcache evictions and worker OOMs in under 3m.

Root cause (working): Interaction between tenant traffic pattern (high short-lived retries + bursty embedding uploads), current kvcache eviction policy and shard-reload backoff leads to GC/eviction thrash and transient worker instability under load.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-13 19:55): Tenant-level throttle and soft-priority-shed decreased error floor. Customer applied client-side retry backoff per guidance.

Engineering fix (in progress): PR github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123 implements kvcache eviction smoothing, increases shard-reload backoff, and makes small-OOM handling graceful to avoid restart loops. Canary scheduled on 2026-03-15 in us-east staging lanes.

Operational follow-ups: 1) Add tenant-specific prewarm suggestions to Console for customers doing mixed embed+chat workloads. 2) Create automated alert for kvcache.evictions/sec > 1000 sustained for 1m. 3) Update runbook with guidance to apply soft ingress caps per-tenant and to ask clients to increase retry backoff to >=500ms for short-lived requests.

Customer communication: Sent status update and mitigation steps to BrightDocs on 2026-03-13 20:30. Will provide postmortem after engineering change is validated. Customer is satisfied with workaround but requests timeline for permanent fix.
Closure criteria: After canary validation and 24h of stable metrics (<0.5% 5xx floor) for BrightDocs tenant in us-east, mark Resolved and schedule postmortem.
